Authority over elders, stand-in for Saint Paul

You don’t trust the holy fathers, you say they were tribal,

Cross-examined by the martyrs — your silence screams defeat
Precedent from centuries you wish you could delete
If each church gets to judge, then truth dissolves to dust
Private verdicts everywhere, nothing you can trust
The gavel strikes “order — the ancient record stands”
Apostolic Succession gave the Scripture in your hands.
⸻

Lawyers for Restoration wave a stack of proof-texts high
Verses deconstructed, no Fathers on their side
“No creed but the Bible!” echoes through the hall

Who guarded every manuscript through torture, flame, and sword?
Who hammered out the Trinity, defending Christ our Lord?

Your entire legal argument, therefore, self-destructs.

Autonomous assemblies — every pastor self-installed
No universal witness — just a thousand voices called

One, holy, universal church, Orthodox in name!

Cross-examined by the martyrs — your silence screams defeat
Precedent from centuries you wish you could delete

Private verdicts everywhere, nothing you can trust
The gavel strikes “order — the ancient record stands”
Apostolic Succession gave the Scripture in your hands.
⸻

Sorin asks the question — answer yes or no:
Did Christ leave His Church? — where did the bishops go?
Did hell prevail for centuries? — did Pentecost just fail?
Did martyrs die for error while your movement set the sail?
The witness stand is shaking — time collapses fast
Restoration’s narrative can’t survive the past.
The jury hears Ignatius — second century cry
The bishops form the backbone — no theory can deny
Your “blackout” doctrine fails — built on shifting sand
Orthodox, unbroken — linked through laying on of hands.
⸻
[Final Chorus]
Cross-examined by the martyrs — your silence screams defeat
Precedent from centuries you wish you could delete
If each church gets to judge, then truth dissolves to dust
Private verdicts everywhere, nothing you can trust
The gavel strikes “order — the ancient record stands”
The Orthodox Church unites God and man.

[Outro]
The jury finds Restoration guilty of fraud.
Sentence, Cross-examination by every saint of God.
Court is adjourned.
February nineteenth — Sorin v. Gallagher — trial continues.

video.title: Does Physicalism Make Knowledge Impossible? | MadeByJimbob vs Leophilius
video.description:
Note: This video features older channel branding that has since been retired as we move toward a more professional debate format. 

Can knowledge exist if physicalism is true?

MadeByJimbob takes the affirmative against Leophilius in a formal debate over whether a purely physical account of reality can adequately explain knowledge, truth, meaning, concepts, intentionality, justification, and our ability to reason about the world.

Jimbob argues that physicalism faces a fundamental ontological problem. If everything that exists is concrete and physical, while categories, propositions, meanings, concepts, truth, justification, and other abstracta are denied independent existence, what exactly are we referring to when we say that someone possesses knowledge? He argues that appealing to brain activity does not by itself explain how a physical state becomes true rather than false, meaningful rather than meaningless, or about one thing rather than another.

Leophilius defends physicalism together with nominalism. He argues that independently existing abstract objects are unnecessary for knowledge. Concepts, categories, mathematical systems, linguistic meanings, and epistemic evaluations do not need to exist as separate objects in reality for physical agents to form beliefs, reason, communicate, and successfully interact with the world. Instead, he appeals to brain processes, emergence, language, shared human practices, and higher-order patterns produced by physical systems.

The debate repeatedly returns to the disagreement over what it means for something to exist. Jimbob argues that denying a positive ontology to concepts, meaning, truth, justification, propositions, and other epistemic tools undermines the very framework required to make knowledge claims. Leophilius argues that nominalism can deny independently existing abstract objects while still allowing physical minds to develop and use conceptual frameworks for understanding reality.

The discussion expands into justified true belief, reliable belief-forming processes, truth-aptness, emergence, brain states, determinism, intentionality, aboutness, foundationalism, Gödel's incompleteness theorems, shared knowledge, biological function, information theory, semantics, natural kinds, mind-independent reality, the law of identity, the nature of logic, and divine conceptualism.

Hosted and moderated by Breakfasttacos.

MEGA BLOODBATH is the home of Breakfasttacos—a creator, host, moderator, and gamer using an animated avatar. The name MEGA BLOODBATH is a metaphor for intense debate, competition, and clashing ideas—not literal violence. We dive deep into theology, ethics, and logic through panels and 1-on-1 debates.

The hosting, moderation, commentary, analysis, creative direction, editing, and production are original to this channel.

video.title: Is Christian Nationalism Good for America? | MadebyJimbob vs Dr. Curt
video.description:
Is Christian Nationalism good for America?

@MadebyJimbob 
​https://substack.com/@ecurtallen

MadebyJimbob and Dr. Curt debate whether Christianity should play a privileged role in American civic life, culture, and government.

MadebyJimbob will defend Christian Nationalism from an Eastern Orthodox Christian perspective. Dr. Curt will argue against Christian Nationalism and challenge whether giving Christianity a special political or cultural status would actually benefit the United States.

A major issue in the debate will be what Christian Nationalism actually means.

For this discussion, MadebyJimbob will defend a conception of Christian Nationalism broadly understood as a cultural and political framework that seeks greater integration of Christianity with American civic life, institutions, values, and public policy, informed specifically by Eastern Orthodox Christianity.

The debate may examine questions including:

• What exactly is Christian Nationalism?

• Should Christianity have a privileged place in American government or public policy?

• What would an Eastern Orthodox Christian political framework actually look like?

• Should government promote specifically Christian moral values?

• Which Christian beliefs should influence law when Christians disagree with one another?

• Can Christian Nationalism protect religious freedom for non-Christians?

• Does Christian Nationalism strengthen American society—or undermine pluralism?

• Can government remain neutral between competing religious traditions?

• Is separation of church and state compatible with a Christian nation?

• What happens when Christian doctrine conflicts with individual liberty?

• Would Christian Nationalism make America more moral, stable, or unified?

• Who gets to determine what counts as authentically Christian public policy?

This debate is not simply about whether Christianity has influenced American history. The central question is whether Christianity should receive a distinctive or privileged role in American civic and political life today.

MadebyJimbob vs Dr. Curt

After the formal debate, the conversation will open for audience questions, challenges, and discussion.

video.title: Is Jesus the "Most High"? || Aelios vs. Fearless Truth — DEBATE #2
video.description:
Is Jesus Christ really the "Most High"?

This is a portion of my second of two debates with Nick, aka Fearless Truth, on whether Latter-day Saints can properly call Jesus the "Most High".

Nick's central challenge is that the LDS model cannot consistently call Jesus the “Most High.” He claims if the Father and Son are not ontologically identical (i.e. if they are genuinely distinct beings), then there cannot be more than one who is properly the Most High God.

My central challenge is simple:

Why should Latter-day Saints have to accept Trinitarian metaphysics in order to call Jesus the “Most High”?

If “Most High” is a title or status that can be shared through divine authority, agency, and investiture, then Jesus need not be numerically or ontologically identical to the Father to properly possess it.

That takes us into ontology and nature, universals and particulars, divine perfection, the meaning of “Most High,” the Monarchy of the Father, divine investiture, premortal existence, creatio ex materia, the grounding of reality and the laws of logic, and eventually creatio ex nihilo and the problem of potentiality.

This was Debate #2 with Nick. Debate #1 "Is the Trinity Logical?" is posted separately.

video.title: Is the Trinity Actually Logical? || Aelios vs. Fearless Truth — DEBATE #1
video.description:
Is the Trinity logical? 

This is a portion of my first of two debates with Nick, aka "Fearless Truth", on the logical coherence of the Trinity.

Nick defends the Trinity using relative identity: the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are distinct as persons while nevertheless being identical as God.

My central challenge is simple:

Does that actually establish the logic of the Trinity—or merely provide a formal schema that can be applied to completely different models?

If the same logical structure can describe the LDS Godhead—or even three distinct humans as “the same human” under some chosen sort—then the syntax alone hasn't captured what is distinctive about the Trinity. Eventually we have to ask what these identity claims actually mean.

That takes us into relative vs. absolute identity, material identity, essence and hypostasis, universals and particulars, the Monarchy of the Father, divine simplicity, and ultimately whether three really distinct persons can each be identical to one numerically identical divine essence without violating classical identity.

This was Debate #1 with Nick. Debate #2 is posted separately.
